name: v3.2.1
body:
## Engram 3.2.1

Core binary publication for v3.2.0 was blocked by obsolete module checksums, although its Cloud image was published. This recovery release fixes the module-tidiness guard without changing resolved dependency versions (#1700). The existing v3.2.0 tag is preserved.

This release brings new, opt-in diagnostics and reliability fixes across the Go core, Cloud replication, setup, and session handling.

### New diagnostics
- Add read-only Pi caller-binding diagnostics to distinguish caller/session evidence from project health, without registering sessions (#1695).
- Add opt-in server-side `mem_save` stage timings to separate save, candidate lookup, and relation insertion costs without logging memory content (#1689). These diagnostics help investigate #1536; they are not a latency fix.

### Fixes
- Preserve ownership metadata when replicating isolated project-owned sessions, and accept legacy blank or omitted directories on mutation pull while keeping chunk import and ownership checks strict (#1662, #1684, #1691).
- Tolerate slow but healthy hook session confirmation with a shared deadline (#1663).
- Scope Cloud upgrade diagnostics to the selected project (#1668).
- Restore Codex resumed-thread memory writes through server-owned continuations (#1612).
- Support explicit `directory` and `cwd` in MCP current-project discovery (#1656).
- Share per-save prompt-capture defaults, opt-out, and deduplication policy in Go (#1696).
- Normalize Unicode project names and support explicit legacy-variant repair (#1694).
- Consistently classify canonical manual-save ownership and repair case-variant session journal rows (#1652, #1678).
- Preserve OpenCode JSONC comments, trailing commas, and unrelated configuration when registering MCP (#1685).
- Refresh existing Claude Code plugins at user scope during setup (#1670).
- Report the actual binary version in the MCP handshake and accurate tool-profile counts (#1675).
- Keep shell scripts LF on Windows checkouts (#1669).

### Maintenance
- Add deterministic perf-ratchet flag, environment, and bootstrap-mode coverage (#1620).

### Upgrade and release scope
- Back up your Engram data and configuration before upgrading, and retain a known-good installation. Ownership corrections can change which sessions are permitted to write.
- This is the **Go core release**. Tag-driven automation publishes Linux, macOS, and Windows archives for amd64/arm64, checksums, the Homebrew formula, and Cloud container images.
- The Pi npm package has a separate release channel and is **not published by this release**. Pi extension changes on `main` are not automatically delivered to npm users.
- This release does not claim to resolve the still-open Pi/Claude resume reports.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v3.1.0...v3.2.1

name: v3.1.0
body:
# Engram 3.1.0

## Highlights
- Add observation version history for topic-key upserts and updates. MCP `mem_get_observation` supports opt-in `include_history`, with pages of up to 50 prior snapshots and `history_cursor` continuation. History is not reconstructed retroactively. (#1286)

## Fixes
- Preserve managed dashboard visibility using project grants, including empty registered projects and canonical names containing spaces or literal percent characters. (#1609, #1630)
- Guard initial Git project binding against conflicting historical directory evidence instead of silently adopting a different scope. (#1596)
- Persist managed-token authentication usage. (#1610)
- Publish identity files atomically on Linux without requiring hard-link support, retaining the compatibility fallback. (#1621)
- Repair titleless queued sync payloads using validated current local observation titles, and improve deferred-relation and identity-repair diagnostics. (#1623, #1611)
- Stop a serving process after permanent database-generation invalidation is observed, with bounded cleanup. This does not retrofit the fix into an already-running older process. (#1646)

## Maintenance
- Simplify OpenCode JSONC setup I/O, dashboard pagination recovery, and CLI export error handling. (#1606, #1615, #1616)
- Expand isolated PostgreSQL, database-generation, and plugin lifecycle coverage. Tests do not establish that every reported runtime incident is fixed. (#1614, #1641, #1643, #1645)

## Upgrade
Back up your database and configuration. Validate compatibility with your integrations, retain a known-good installation, and restart long-running Engram servers and MCP processes to use the new binary. Go source consumers continue to use the `/v3` module path.

## Release scope and known limitations
This is the core binary release. It does not publish a new `gentle-engram` npm package; npm remains at 0.2.0, and newer Pi changes on main are not delivered by this core tag. Open resume reports #1622, #1635, #1624, and #1593 are not claimed resolved.

Thanks to @josegarvinvictoria, @Reaan06, and @dnlrsls for the merged contributions.

The comparison includes Pi source changes; their presence here does not imply a new npm release.

name: v3.0.0
body:
Engram 3.0.0 is a major release. It requires an explicit `expected_project` for every observation update and delete, moves the Go module path to `/v3`, adds OpenCode 2.x support, and confirms host-session registration before agent integrations bind memory writes. This tag publishes the **core binary**; the Pi package `gentle-engram` has a separate npm release channel (details below).

## What changed since v2.2.1

### Agent integrations and session attribution

- Add OpenCode 2.x support through a dual-major plugin entrypoint: the same handlers serve the V1 `server` entry and the V2 `setup` entry, and CI now runs the OpenCode plugin tests ([#1526](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1526)).
- Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode confirm the host session's registration before binding classified Engram writes and prompt capture, and deny failed, ended, or mismatched registrations instead of persisting to a stale session ([#1478](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1478), [#1513](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1513), [#1479](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1479), [#1521](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1521), [#1488](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1488)). The Claude Code plugin is released under new versions so existing installations receive the session-binding hook ([#1518](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1518), [#1571](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1571)).
- `POST /sessions` accepts `resume: true`: when the requested session has ended, the core reuses a live `<id>:resume:N` continuation or creates the next one atomically, and never reopens ended sessions. OpenCode uses it to keep capturing after restarts and reloads ([#1564](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1564)).
- OpenCode validates session acknowledgements, surfaces deduplicated degraded-operation warnings in tool results, forwards V2 `session.updated` events, and lets explicit writes from an ambiguous multi-repo directory reach MCP recovery ([#1572](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1572), [#1573](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1573), [#1576](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1576)).
- `engram setup codex` no longer writes `model_instructions_file` or `experimental_compact_prompt_file`, which replaced Codex's built-in instructions, and removes them when a previous version wrote them ([#1550](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1550)). On Windows, the Codex session-start hook starts a missing local server detached from the hook pipes ([#1538](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1538)).
- `engram setup pi` no longer registers an Engram MCP server or installs `pi-mcp-adapter`; existing entries are preserved and reported ([#1475](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1475), [#1578](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1578)).
- The server advertises `capabilities.isolated_session_registration` and rejects isolated registrations that conflict with an existing session's directory without changing that session ([#1592](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1592)).

### Memory, projects, and MCP

- `mem_get_observation` accepts an optional `project` for response context and falls back to the observation's stored project when the working directory is ambiguous; retrieval stays ID-based ([#1444](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1444), [#1490](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1490)).
- Add `engram projects merge` with `--dry-run` and `--apply` for one explicitly named separator-variant merge; merges into the reserved `inbox` project are rejected ([#1457](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1457)).
- Preserve prompt inbox identity through sync, backup export, and import, so deleted prompt identities cannot reappear ([#1464](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1464)).
- Ambiguous-project errors list available projects in alphabetical order ([#1565](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1565)).
- Project names detected from Git remotes decode one layer of URL encoding (for example, Azure DevOps `My%20Project`), matching `engram cloud enroll`; `--literal-project` preserves percent-encoded names. Existing stored repository bindings are reused as-is ([#1590](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1590)).

### Sync, Cloud, and doctor repairs

- Apply a superseded session delete at its original chunk position, so chunks that delete and recreate a session no longer stall on a foreign-key failure ([#1520](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1520)).
- Include legacy blank-project session mutations in Cloud upgrade diagnosis and repair; Cloud export stops until they are repaired ([#1528](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1528)).
- Report session-index failures instead of acknowledging an identical Cloud chunk replay as successful ([#1474](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1474)).
- Preserve paused autosync status when an in-progress cycle completes or fails ([#1592](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1592)).
- Add the `orphaned_pending_relations` doctor check and a backup-first `engram doctor repair --check orphaned_pending_relations` route; `engram conflicts stats` reports orphaned relations ([#1472](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1472)).
- Add `engram doctor discard-empty-prompt` to preview or discard an irrecoverable legacy empty prompt mutation; applying requires a backup path ([#1579](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1579)).

### Obsidian, build, and CI

- The Obsidian plugin consumes `GET /export` observations as full snapshots instead of silently accepting an incompatible payload, and its build and typecheck are reproducible in CI ([#1487](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1487), [#1486](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1486)).
- CI runs the existing policy and Obsidian regression suites; the dead-code analyzer uses the module's Go toolchain; manual Pi publication validates the full tag ref ([#1517](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1517), [#1570](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1570), [#1473](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1473)).

## Breaking and compatibility changes

### Go module path

Source consumers must use the v3 module path ([#1598](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1598)):

```bash
go install github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v3/cmd/engram@v3.0.0
```

Code importing `github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2/...` packages must update its import paths to `/v3`.

### Observation updates and deletes require `expected_project`

Every caller must assert the observation's owner before mutating it ([#1575](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1575)):

- **HTTP:** `PATCH /observations/{id}` and `DELETE /observations/{id}` require `?expected_project=<project>`. A missing, blank, or invalid value returns `400`; an owner mismatch returns `409`; a missing observation returns `404`. A rejected request changes no observation, revision, or sync queue entry.
- **MCP:** `mem_update` and `mem_delete` require an explicit `expected_project` argument. `mem_update` no longer falls back to the stored owner when the working directory is ambiguous; `mem_get_observation` keeps that fallback for reads.
- **Pi:** the Pi-native `mem_update` and `mem_delete` tools require the same argument; see the Pi section below.

`expected_project` is a caller assertion, not authentication or tenant isolation. CLI and internal maintenance paths are unchanged.

### Agent setup behavior

- `engram setup pi` no longer creates an Engram MCP entry or installs `npm:pi-mcp-adapter`. Pi 0.99.0 and later include built-in MCP for other servers; an installed `/mcp` extension replaces it. Remove a retained `mcpServers.engram` entry manually for native-only writes ([#1475](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1475), [#1578](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1578)).
- Claude Code SessionStart no longer runs MCP registration. Register or repair it with `engram setup claude-code` ([#1571](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1571)).
- `engram setup codex` removes legacy instruction-file override keys from the Codex config ([#1550](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1550)).

## Pi 0.2.0 on npm

`engram setup pi` on this tag installs [`gentle-engram` 0.2.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gentle-engram/v/0.2.0), published from tag [`pi-v0.2.0`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/releases/tag/pi-v0.2.0), and upgrades existing `gentle-engram` 0.1.16 declarations ([#1604](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1604)). Pi 0.2.0 sends `expected_project`; Pi 0.1.16 does not, so a v3.0.0 server rejects its `mem_update` and `mem_delete` calls with `400`. Rerun `engram setup pi`, or update an existing Pi installation directly:

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.2.0
pi-engram init
```

Restart Pi afterward.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up your local database and configuration. Keep the SQLite database on a **local filesystem**.
2. Upgrade the core binary with a release archive or Homebrew; verify manual downloads against `checksums.txt`. Source installs use the `/v3` module path shown above.
3. Update every HTTP and MCP client that updates or deletes observations to send `expected_project`.
4. Run `engram doctor` and follow only the guidance applicable to your store.
5. Rerun `engram setup codex` to remove legacy instruction overrides, and `engram setup claude-code` if Claude Code's MCP registration is missing.
6. Restart long-running MCP and agent sessions to pick up the new binary. If you use Pi, rerun `engram setup pi` or install `gentle-engram` 0.2.0 as shown above.

## Known limitations accepted for this release

- **Hook-based session attribution:** registration confirmation runs inside agent hooks. Skipped, bypassed, or timed-out hooks are not protected, and direct or manual MCP saves are outside this guard.
- **OpenCode 2.x late parent attribution:** delayed parent attribution through V2 `session.updated` is covered by regression tests but has not been verified in a live runtime.
- **Network filesystems:** remote filesystems identified at startup are still rejected, and unknown mounts are not proof of safety. Use local storage and retain backups.

## Installation and full comparison

Release archives cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64, alongside `checksums.txt`. See the complete core diff in [`v2.2.1...v3.0.0`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v2.2.1...v3.0.0).

name: gentle-engram v0.2.0
body:
## What's Changed

- **Breaking:** Pi-native `mem_update` and `mem_delete` require an explicit `expected_project` argument and forward it to Engram's `PATCH` and `DELETE /observations/{id}` routes. Missing, invalid, or mismatched owners are rejected without changing the observation (#1575).
- `pi-engram init` configures Pi-native `mem_*` tools without creating or replacing an Engram MCP registration. An existing `mcpServers.engram` entry is preserved and reported with its config path; remove it manually and reload Pi for native-only writes (#1476).
- `pi-engram init` no longer installs or declares `npm:pi-mcp-adapter`. Pi 0.99.0 and later include built-in MCP for other servers; existing adapter entries are left untouched (#1578).
- Pi startup no longer silently imports tracked `.engram/manifest.json` chunks from a cloned repository. Run `engram sync --import` from the checkout to import them (#1456).
- Explicit cross-project `project` or `cwd` saves use an isolated, project-owned session instead of conflicting with the current session's ownership (#1592).
- Resumed sessions register with `resume: true` and adopt the session ID acknowledged by the core; existing `:resume:<uuid>` mappings keep working (#1581).
- `mem_context` accepts optional `max_bytes` (capped at 64 KiB) and `compact` arguments (#1447).
- `mem_session_end` accepts only the current Pi host session ID and refuses foreign, missing, or empty IDs before any end request (#1477).
- Automatic prompt capture redacts `<private>` blocks before truncating to 2,000 characters (#1559).
- Background-capture warnings appear in the owning Pi UI instead of raw stderr over the editor; headless and print modes keep stderr diagnostics (#1574).
- The Memory Protocol is appended through `systemPromptOptions.appendSystemPrompt` when Pi provides it, so turns started with `triggerTurn` keep it; older Pi versions keep the previous behavior (#1589).
- A server launched by the plugin starts with Cloud autosync enabled, matching the Claude Code and Codex launchers (#1587).
- TypeBox is now an optional wildcard peer provided by Pi instead of a bundled dependency (#1567).

## Install

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.2.0
pi-engram init
```

Restart Pi afterward.

## Notes

- Requires Engram v3.0.0 or later for `expected_project` updates and deletes, `resume` registration of ended sessions, and isolated cross-project saves (`capabilities.isolated_session_registration`). Older servers refuse resumed and cross-project registrations with a specific cause instead of a guessed session.
- `engram setup pi` in core v3.0.0 installs this version and upgrades existing `gentle-engram@0.1.16` declarations.

## Verification

- `node test/release-contract.mjs refs/tags/pi-v0.2.0` from `plugin/pi`
- `cd plugin/pi && npm test`

Published to npm via GitHub Actions with provenance.

name: v2.2.1
body:
Engram 2.2.1 is a patch release focused on session-identity repair, `engram doctor`, setup path stability, and hook capture reliability. This tag publishes the **core binary**; the Pi package `gentle-engram` 0.1.16 was published separately on npm (details below).

## What changed since v2.2.0

### Session identity and doctor repairs

- Add an explicit, backup-backed repair for legacy blank session IDs: `engram doctor repair --check invalid_session_identity --replacement-id <canonical-id>` migrates the session with its observations and prompts atomically. Plan and dry-run stay nonmutating, and publication counts report only corrected current-state mutations ([#1401](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1401), [#1406](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1406), [#1409](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1409), [#1416](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1416)).
- Reject historical journal mutations with duplicate source identifiers before identity repair deletes the source session ([#1436](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1436)).
- Backfill missing `directory` fields in eligible pending session mutations on local-only installs, so they enter the repair plan instead of staying pending ([#1443](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1443)).
- Allow `mem_merge_projects` to merge explicitly named `-`/`_` separator variants without loosening automatic consolidation ([#1415](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1415)).

### Server health

- Local `/health` now checks the live backing store, and stats propagate SQL errors instead of returning misleading zero counts; failures return a generic HTTP 500 ([#1418](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1418)).
- A same-instance `engram serve` that cannot bind its port now logs one diagnostic instead of exiting silently; systemd guidance recommends `Restart=on-failure` ([#1405](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1405)).

### Agent setup and hooks

- `engram setup` records mise's stable shim (`<mise-data-dir>/shims/engram`) instead of a versioned install path, so MCP registrations survive `mise up` and `mise prune`. `engram setup pi` can repair an `mcpServers.engram` entry whose absolute command no longer exists ([#1425](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1425)).
- Codex setup and the native Windows hook use the absolute `CODEX_HOME` when set, otherwise `~/.codex` ([#1410](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1410)).
- Claude Code SubagentStop capture preserves multiline content on Windows and Unix, and Claude Code/Codex hooks fall back to `stdout` when the subagent message is explicitly empty ([#1402](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1402), [#1433](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1433)).
- `engram setup pi` now installs `npm:gentle-engram@0.1.16` and migrates older pins, including 0.1.14 and 0.1.15 ([#1448](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1448)).

## Pi 0.1.16 on npm

[`gentle-engram` 0.1.16](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gentle-engram/v/0.1.16) is published with npm provenance from tag `pi-v0.1.16`. It includes the fix for memory writes after resuming a quit Pi session (`pi --continue`) ([#1387](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1387)), and `pi-engram init` now migrates 0.1.14 and 0.1.15 pins. To update an existing Pi installation:

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.1.16
pi-engram init
```

Restart Pi afterward.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up your local database and configuration. Keep the SQLite database on a **local filesystem**.
2. Upgrade the core binary with a release archive or Homebrew; verify manual downloads against `checksums.txt`.
3. Run `engram doctor`. If it reports `invalid_session_identity`, follow the documented repair with an explicit canonical `--replacement-id`; run plan/dry-run first.
4. If you installed Engram through mise, rerun `engram setup <agent>` once so MCP registrations point at the stable shim.
5. Restart long-running MCP and agent sessions to pick up the new binary. If you use Pi, update its npm package as shown above.

## Known limitations accepted for this release

- **Cloned repositories and Pi:** [#1445](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1445) reports that a cloned repository can silently import tracked memories into the global store. It is open and not addressed here.
- **Network filesystems:** remote filesystems identified at startup are still rejected, and unknown mounts are not proof of safety. Use local storage and retain backups.

## Installation and full comparison

Release archives cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64, alongside `checksums.txt`. See the complete core diff in [`v2.2.0...v2.2.1`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v2.2.0...v2.2.1).

name: v2.2.0
body:
Engram 2.2.0 adds CommandCode setup and strengthens local-data safety, project identity, Windows agent hooks, and diagnostics. This tag publishes the **core binary**; the Pi package `gentle-engram` has a separate npm release channel.

## What changed since v2.1.0

### Memory and local data integrity

- Refuse SQLite WAL startup on filesystems identified as remote, with platform-specific detection and regression coverage. Keep the database on a **local filesystem**: unclassified mounts are not certified safe ([#1364](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1364), [#1365](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1365)).
- Preserve blank-directory sessions and their dependent records during local import, and apply same-project relation guards across endpoint scopes ([#1298](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1298), [#1374](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1374)).
- Resolve the canonical identity of an unambiguous promoted child Git repository; atomically claim ownership only for the narrow ended, unowned legacy-session registration case. Neither change is a general automatic session repair ([#1395](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1395), [#1400](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1400)).
- Index project-scoped exports to avoid broad scans of sessions, observations, and prompts ([#1379](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1379)).

### Agent setup and CLI

- Add `engram setup commandcode` for CommandCode's user-scope MCP configuration and Memory Protocol ([#1123](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1123)).
- Restore Codex Windows prompt/startup hook routing, bind Codex MCP writes to their runtime session, and preserve UTF-8 session IDs ([#1377](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1377), [#1367](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1367), [#1366](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1366), [#1363](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1363)).
- Diagnose stale absolute Engram executable paths in supported MCP registrations without changing them automatically; `engram doctor` names the affected client and its explicit `engram setup <agent>` recovery step. Export/import help no longer triggers setup side effects ([#1394](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1394), [#1369](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1369)).
- Accept implicit stdio MCP registration in Claude Code and select the OpenCode V1 plugin entrypoint explicitly ([#1385](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1385), [#1389](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1389)).

### Dashboard and build reliability

- Render dashboard timestamps in the configured `ENGRAM_TIMEZONE`, falling back to local time without changing stored UTC values ([#1384](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1384)).
- Pin and scope templ generation to dashboard sources so generated output stays aligned with its templates ([#1386](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1386), [#1397](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1397)).

## Pi 0.1.15 is a separate release

The core's `engram setup pi` path pins [`gentle-engram` 0.1.15 on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gentle-engram/v/0.1.15). Pi source changes on this core tag do **not** publish a newer npm package. To update an existing Pi installation to the published package:

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.1.15
```

Restart Pi afterward. Pi project listing needs an Engram server at least v2.1.0; see the [compatibility guidance](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1399). The separate fix for writes after resuming a quit Pi session remains open in [#1376](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1376); do not treat it as part of this core release.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up your local database and configuration. Keep the SQLite database on a **local filesystem**, not NFS or another network mount.
2. Upgrade the core binary with a release archive or Homebrew; verify manual downloads against `checksums.txt`.
3. Run `engram doctor` and follow only the guidance applicable to your store. Restart long-running MCP and agent sessions to pick up the new binary.
4. If you use Pi, update its npm package separately as needed and restart Pi.

## Known limitations accepted for this release

- **Network filesystem data safety:** [#1292](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1292) remains open. Positively identified remote filesystems are rejected at startup; unknown filesystems are not proof of safety. Use local storage and retain backups.
- **Legacy session identity repair:** [#1332](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1332) remains open. The narrow ownership claim above is not the requested operator-facing canonical-ID repair flow.
- **Pi quit/resume writes:** [#1376](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1376) remains open; the Pi fix is not in the published npm 0.1.15 package.
- **Occupied server port:** [#1391](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1391) reports silent `engram serve` exit when another Engram process using the same instance already owns the port; this report is not described as fixed here.

## Installation and full comparison

Release archives cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64, alongside `checksums.txt`; the stable Homebrew formula is at 2.2.0. See the complete core diff in [`v2.1.0...v2.2.0`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v2.1.0...v2.2.0). The Pi package has its own npm version and source tag.

name: v2.1.0
body:
Engram 2.1.0 builds on the v2 foundation with atomic observation replacements, more reliable local storage and Cloud synchronization, and safer agent integrations. This tag publishes the **core binary**. The Pi package `gentle-engram` 0.1.15 was published separately after this core tag; see [Pi 0.1.15](#pi-0115-is-a-separate-release) below.

## What changed since v2.0.0

### Memory and local data integrity

- Added atomic literal find-and-replace for existing observations through the validated MCP and HTTP contracts ([#1342](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1342)).
- Acquired SQLite write locks at transaction start to avoid `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` failures in read-then-write transactions, and upgraded the SQLite runtime with the upstream WAL-reset integrity fix ([#1243](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1243), [#1308](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1308)). These fixes do **not** make network filesystems safe for the database; see [#1292](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1292).
- Added a confirmed, local-only `doctor repair` path for observations whose parent session is missing; diagnostics now distinguish repairable findings from informational checks ([#1268](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1268), [#1265](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1265)).

### Cloud and sync convergence

- Materialized mutation-only session, observation, and prompt uploads; preserved local hard-delete tombstones during export ([#1312](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1312), [#1313](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1313)).
- Continued pulling remote changes when enrollment blocks a push, and deferred pulled records only when their parent session is verifiably absent ([#1309](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1309), [#1274](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1274)).

### Agent integrations

- Added a native Codex user-prompt hook command and tightened executable selection. **Windows adapter activation and end-to-end timeout verification are not included**; [#1271](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1271) remains open for v2.2.0 ([#1356](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1356), [#1354](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1354)).
- Bound supported Claude Code writes to their runtime session and added a declarative `engram setup kimi` adapter for Kimi Code CLI ([#1352](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1352), [#793](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/793)).
- Improved Pi detection of legacy pre-v2 servers and bounded retry timing in the package bundled with this core tag ([#1279](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1279)).

## Pi 0.1.15 is a separate release

[`gentle-engram` 0.1.15 on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gentle-engram/v/0.1.15) ([`pi-v0.1.15` source tag](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/tree/pi-v0.1.15)) improves transport timeout handling for [#1272](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1272): bounded read retries, a write timeout budget that accommodates slower writes, and explicit unknown outcomes when a write may already have been applied. It does not silently retry uncertain writes.

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.1.15
```

The **v2.1.0 core tag still pins Pi 0.1.14** in its bundled setup command. Install Pi 0.1.15 explicitly if you need this patch; it is not part of the v2.1.0 core archives.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up your local database and configuration. Keep the SQLite database on a **local filesystem**, not NFS/network storage.
2. Upgrade the core binary with the release archive or Homebrew; verify the archive against `checksums.txt` when downloading manually.
3. Run `engram doctor` and follow only the repair guidance applicable to your store. Restart long-running agent and MCP sessions to load the new binary.
4. If you use Pi, install `gentle-engram` 0.1.15 separately with the command above and restart Pi.

## Known limitations accepted for this release

- **Network filesystem data safety:** [#1292](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1292) — placing the local SQLite database on NFS/network storage can cause WAL corruption. Use a local filesystem and retain backups.
- **Export/import:** [#1287](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1287) — exports with blank session directories can fail to import.
- **Windows sync:** [#1175](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1175) — a large multi-project database can make local sync hang.
- **Contributor code generation:** [#1260](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1260) — documented `go tool templ generate` fails without a tool directive; use `make templ` instead.
- **Windows Codex hook:** [#1271](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1271) — its existing shell adapter can still exceed the two-second timeout. The native command added in #1356 is not yet wired on Windows; adapter activation and end-to-end timeout verification are deferred to v2.2.0.

## Installation and full comparison

Release archives cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64, with `checksums.txt`; the stable Homebrew formula is also at 2.1.0. See the full core diff in [`v2.0.0...v2.1.0`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v2.0.0...v2.1.0). The Pi patch has its own tag and npm provenance.

name: v2.0.0
body:
Engram 2.0.0 is the first stable release of the v2 line. It contains 462 commits since v1.20.0 across project-aware memory, agent integrations, relation-aware retrieval, optional Cloud replication, managed access, diagnostics, and data-integrity hardening.

## What changed since v1.20.0

### Project-aware memory and ownership

- Project identity is resolved consistently from explicit configuration, `ENGRAM_PROJECT`, Git metadata, and the current directory.
- Added `mem_current_project`, project listing/consolidation/pruning, project merging, explicit global reads, and legacy ownership rescue tooling.
- Runtime-bound session attribution prevents writes from being assigned to the wrong session, project, worktree, or agent process.
- Project-scoped reads now behave consistently across CLI, MCP, HTTP, export, review, Obsidian export, and sync status.

### Richer local memory and retrieval

- Added curated prompt capture, topic-key upserts, duplicate/revision tracking, review cycles, local pinning, context-size limits, UTF-8-safe truncation, and compact context output.
- Expanded FTS5 search with project and scope filters, match modes, topic-key results, and CJK/trigram support.
- Added `engram doctor`, expanded project-management commands, improved the Bubble Tea TUI, and introduced beta Obsidian knowledge-graph export.
- Backup export/import now preserves pinned observations and memory relations.

### Conflict detection and memory relations

- `mem_save` can surface likely conflicting memories for review.
- Added `mem_judge` and `mem_compare` for persisted verdicts including `supersedes`, `conflicts_with`, `compatible`, and `not_conflict`.
- Search results expose stable relation annotations.
- CLI and local HTTP surfaces support conflict listing, scanning, statistics, inspection, and deferred-relation replay.
- Relation judgments participate in local, Git, and Cloud synchronization with dependency-aware deferral.

### Agent integrations and session safety

- Expanded setup and integration coverage for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Kiro, Kilo Code, Qwen Code, Windsurf, and other MCP clients.
- Added thin plugin and hook integrations for session lifecycle, compaction recovery, passive capture, prompt capture, and Memory Protocol injection.
- Hardened Pi cross-project write protection, shutdown handling, package compatibility, error reporting, and installer/package-version parity.
- Published `gentle-engram@0.1.13`, matching the version installed by `engram setup pi`.
- The OpenCode 1.x adapter now works in Node-hosted plugin environments without relying on Bun globals.

### Optional Cloud replication and autosync

- Added the optional `engram cloud serve` runtime with Postgres-backed storage, project enrollment, compressed chunk transport, mutation push/pull, and deterministic reason codes.
- Added opt-in autosync for `engram serve` and `engram mcp`, with lease protection, bounded retries, exponential backoff, degraded-state reporting, and graceful shutdown.
- Added project-scoped Cloud upgrade commands: `doctor`, `repair`, `bootstrap`, `status`, and pre-verification rollback.
- Added per-target tombstone floors and offline reconciliation for unenrolled legacy journal entries.
- Local SQLite remains authoritative; Cloud remains optional replication and browser visibility.

### Cloud dashboard and managed access

- Added server-rendered project, session, observation, prompt, contributor, health, sync-control, audit, and managed-user dashboard surfaces.
- Added managed principals, human users, project grants, token issuance/revocation, first-admin bootstrap, and audit logging.
- Added dedicated managed-token hashing through `ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN_PEPPER`.
- Dashboard reads now enforce the authenticated principal’s project grants instead of relying only on the deployment allowlist.
- Existing `ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN` and `ENGRAM_CLOUD_ADMIN` credentials remain available as a legacy fallback.

### Reliability and data-integrity hardening

- Added safe planning and explicit partial outcomes for legacy ownership repair.
- Hardened nullable legacy-session handling across store reads, export, deletion, lifecycle operations, and diagnostics.
- Added doctor findings for unowned sessions and orphaned observation/session references.
- Rejected titleless observations before side effects, preventing poisoned mutation queues.
- Hardened sync ordering, mutation payload validation, CJK migrations, UTF-8 truncation, autosync shutdown, and SQLite generation boundaries.
- Added Obsidian export path-containment protection.
- Made Cloud push limits configurable while preserving the 8 MiB default.
- `doctor repair` now distinguishes repairable checks from diagnostic-only checks and prints executable continuations.

## Breaking and compatibility changes

### Go module path

Source consumers must use the v2 module path:

```bash
go install github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2/cmd/engram@latest
```

### Read scoping

Omitted project selectors now resolve the canonical current project instead of implicitly reading every project. Use `--all` or `all_projects=true` only when a global read is intentional.

### Project resolution

Ambiguous current-directory detection now fails with available-project information. Configure `.engram/config.json`, set `ENGRAM_PROJECT`, move into the intended repository, or pass an explicit project.

### Cloud scope and authentication

- Cloud sync remains explicitly project-scoped; `engram sync --cloud --all` is rejected.
- Cloud servers require `ENGRAM_CLOUD_ALLOWED_PROJECTS`.
- Authenticated deployments require a non-default `ENGRAM_JWT_SECRET`.
- `ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN_PEPPER` enables managed-token authentication and must be distinct from `ENGRAM_JWT_SECRET`. Without it, legacy Cloud credentials continue to work.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up `~/.engram/engram.db`.
2. Upgrade Engram through Homebrew or a release archive.
3. Run `engram doctor` and follow any reported repair path.
4. Restart long-running MCP servers and agent sessions so they load the v2 binary and contracts.
5. Pi users should rerun `engram setup pi` if their installation still resolves an older `gentle-engram` package.
6. For enrolled Cloud projects, follow the Cloud `doctor` → `repair` → `bootstrap` upgrade sequence instead of assuming an implicit remote migration.

## Known limitations

- [#1242](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1242): a stale OpenCode root session can still make omitted-session `mem_save` fail closed. End the stale session or provide the intended `session_id`.
- [#1220](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1220): the dedicated OpenCode 2.x adapter is not included; `engram setup opencode` targets OpenCode 1.x.
- [#1182](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1182): concurrent processes can still encounter SQLite write contention and transient MCP connectivity loss.
- [#1135](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1135): a permanently unsatisfiable relation dependency can stall Cloud import convergence.
- [#1175](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1175): local sync can become pathologically slow on very large stores containing extensive duplicate history.

## Installation

Release archives include Linux, macOS, and Windows builds for amd64 and arm64 plus `checksums.txt`. The stable tag also updates the Homebrew formula.

## Full comparison

See every commit in [`v1.20.0...v2.0.0`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v1.20.0...v2.0.0).

name: v2.0.0-rc.12
body:
## Engram v2.0.0-rc.12

This release candidate focuses on sync integrity, agent lifecycle reliability, safer Cloud behavior, and more complete MCP and plugin contracts.

> This is a prerelease intended for validation before the final v2.0.0 release. Please report regressions through the [issue tracker](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues).

### Highlights

#### Sync and data integrity

- Prevented unenrolled projects from accumulating an unpushable Cloud journal backlog.
- Coalesced pending session upserts and repaired foreign sync targets.
- Hard-deleted soft-deleted observations when required by the sync lifecycle.
- Scoped pulled relation endpoints by project and hardened relation handling across replicas.
- Prevented Unicode topic-key collisions.

#### Agent and runtime reliability

- Closed OpenCode sub-agent and misregistered sessions across lifecycle signals.
- Propagated confirmed Codex runtime session identity and made Windows shell hooks non-interactive.
- Closed Pi sessions on shutdown and prevented cross-project session writes.
- Made MCP exit gracefully when its parent pipe closes and terminate Windows workers with their parent.
- Added diagnostics for ambiguous active sessions and improved manual-session target selection.

#### Cloud and transport safety

- Recovered stranded bootstrap tokens.
- Rejected non-UTF-8 mutation payloads.
- Audited denied authentication attempts.
- Accepted gzip mutation pushes regardless of `Content-Type`.

#### CLI, MCP, and plugin contracts

- Added `engram init` for ambiguous workspaces.
- Reported save truncation and skipped update checks during `doctor`.
- Included non-empty `topic_key` values in normal and compact MCP search results.
- Advanced the Claude hook package version identity so existing installs can receive the SessionStart fix.

### Known limitations before stable

- Older pulled upserts can still resurrect deleted entities when they bypass the tombstone sequence floor ([#1197](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1197)).
- Dependency-safe import and pull still have unresolved hard-stop cases ([#1135](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1135), [#1166](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1166)).
- Large Windows databases can still trigger an indefinitely running sync, and concurrent agents can still encounter SQLite lock failures ([#1175](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1175), [#1182](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1182)).
- Claude Code hook setup does not yet enforce every external hook dependency ([#1133](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1133)).
- CLI project parsing and release-install detection still have open edge cases ([#1205](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1205), [#1194](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1194)).
- Organization propagation through passive capture remains incomplete ([#1152](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1152)).

### Downloads

Release assets include Linux, macOS, and Windows archives for `amd64` and `arm64`. Verify downloads with `checksums.txt`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/compare/v2.0.0-rc.11...v2.0.0-rc.12

name: v2.0.0-rc.11
body:
## Engram v2.0.0-rc.11

This release candidate consolidates search quality improvements, safer Cloud lifecycle behavior, bounded MCP output, plugin/server reliability fixes, and repository governance hardening.

> This is a prerelease intended for validation before the final v2.0.0 release. Please report regressions through the [issue tracker](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues).

### Highlights

#### Search and retrieval
- Added deterministic composite search reranking using pinned, recency, and revision-stability signals while preserving lexical BM25 dominance ([#958](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/958), [#1148](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1148)).
- Exposed the existing `all`/`any` search semantics through `engram search --match` ([#861](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/861), [#1124](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1124)).

#### Cloud and sync
- Added progress reporting for Cloud imports, including local, remote, and pending counts ([#984](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/984), [#1147](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1147)).
- Added Cloud inbox foundations: a reserved sync target, telemetry exclusion, and closed-space diagnostics ([#1091](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1091), [#1098](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1098)).
- Made rejected Cloud mutations identifiable and observable without exposing payload contents ([#779](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/779), [#1146](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1146)).
- Added `cloud unenroll` and `cloud config --clear`, with accurate effective configuration status ([#1114](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1114), [#1130](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1130)).

#### MCP, plugins, and runtime reliability
- Bounded complete `mem_context` responses, including Unicode, tiny-budget, and no-context edge cases ([#1039](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1039), [#1074](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1074)).
- Added a non-blocking warning when `mem_save` content contains absolute filesystem paths ([#1087](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1087), [#1143](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1143)).
- Isolated managed server instances by data directory, preventing duplicate startup and cross-user attachment on the shared port ([#1100](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1100), [#1120](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1120), [#1127](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1127)).
- Restored deferred memory-tool exposure for Claude and added SessionEnd cleanup ([#1077](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1077), [#1139](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1139), [#1132](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1132)).
- Extended the SQLite write-retry window for transient contention ([#1129](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1129)).

#### Repository governance
- Added trusted-base checks that reject transient development artifacts in pull requests ([#1093](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1093), [#1128](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1128)).
- Defined and enforced a canonical issue and pull-request label taxonomy ([#1115](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1115), [#1137](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1137)).

### Known limitations before stable

- Sync-journal repair and false-success diagnostics remain open in [#1026](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1026) and [#1104](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1104).
- [#1142](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1142) still requires deployment/request evidence before an Engram-side fix can be confirmed.
- [#886](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/886) remains paused pending host-side process evidence.
- [#1013](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/1013) remains open; this RC includes its Cloud inbox foundation slice, not the complete feature.
